title: Nylon vs Polyester vs Triexta vs Wool Carpet: Which Fiber Should You Buy?
meta: Nylon vs polyester vs triexta vs wool carpet: nylon and triexta for busy Sammamish homes, polyester for bedrooms, wool for looks. Guide by Wills Flooring.
keywords: nylon vs polyester carpet, triexta vs nylon carpet, wool vs nylon carpet, best carpet fiber for family, which carpet fiber is most durable, carpet installation Sammamish WA

blocks.lead: For a busy Sammamish household with kids and a dog, buy nylon or triexta. Polyester is the value pick for bedrooms and low-traffic rooms, and wool is the premium pick when you want the best look and feel and can keep pet accidents off it.
blocks.detail: Fiber decides how a carpet wears, how it handles stains and how it feels. Density and pad decide the rest. Installation labor is the same $0.99 per sq ft whichever fiber you choose, so the fiber only moves the material line. We bring all four to your house so you can compare them on your own floor.

blocks.html: Every carpet store sells the same four fibers under a hundred brand names, and the pitch usually leans toward whatever is on promotion. Fiber is the single most important choice you make about a carpet, more than color or style, because it decides whether the upstairs hall in your Klahanie or Trossachs house still looks good after eight years of soccer cleats and a golden retriever. Here is how the four compare with the marketing stripped away.

items.title: Nylon
items.text: Nylon has the best resilience of any synthetic: the fibers bend under foot and spring back for years, which is why it resists matting in halls and on stairs. It is not naturally stain resistant and relies on a topical treatment that wears off, so spills need quick attention. Type 6,6 is the premium version. Expect twelve to fifteen years in a family home.

items.title: Polyester (PET)
items.text: Polyester is inherently stain resistant, takes bright colors and is often made from recycled bottles. It costs the least of the four. Its weakness is resilience: the fibers crush and mat in traffic lanes, so a plush polyester in a busy hall looks tired in five to seven years. Excellent in bedrooms and guest rooms.

items.title: Triexta (PTT)
items.text: Triexta is a polyester cousin engineered to fix polyester's problems. Its stain resistance is permanent and built into the fiber, it is soft, and its resilience sits close enough to nylon for most homes. It is partly corn-based. Oily soil is harder to clean out of it, and it costs about what mid-grade nylon does.

items.title: Wool
items.text: Wool is naturally resilient, flame resistant, hides soil well and can last twenty-five years. It feels and looks like nothing else. It is also the most expensive fiber, absorbs moisture, is damaged by pet urine and harsh cleaners, and sheds for the first months. It wants a firm pad and a dry room.

A 1,400 sq ft upstairs in Klahanie with 16 stairs is 1,400 x $0.99 + 16 x $30 = $1,386 + $480 = $1,866 in labor. Wool or polyester, that number is identical. What changes is the carpet and pad quote, which we write up with the samples on your floor.

blocks.text: Fiber by room in a Sammamish plateau home

items.text: The hardest-working carpet in the house. Nylon, in a dense cut pile or a tight loop, over a firm pad. Triexta is a fine second choice. Skip polyester here; the traffic lane will show first.
Spills, markers and the occasional sick night. Triexta's built-in stain resistance earns its keep here, and it is soft enough for floor play. A patterned or flecked style hides what does get through.
Big, often cooler, used for movies and sleepovers. A dense polyester frieze is a sensible value choice: the room is used hard but not walked through constantly, so matting is less of an issue.

items.d: Main bedroom and formal living room
items.text: Low traffic, high expectations. This is where wool or a soft premium nylon makes sense. Keep the dog's bed elsewhere if you choose wool, and use a flat rubber or fiber pad.
Wet dog from Beaver Lake or Pine Lake, muddy cleats from the trail. Solution-dyed nylon or triexta in a mid-tone, with a moisture-barrier pad so accidents do not reach the subfloor.

blocks.text: Nylon or triexta? The question we get most

a.title: Pick nylon when
items: Stairs and halls carry most of the traffic
You want the longest proven track record for resilience
You are fine renewing a stain treatment after professional cleaning
You prefer a slightly crisper, less silky hand

b.title: Pick triexta when
items: Young kids and pets make stains the bigger worry than matting
You want softness without giving up much durability
You do not want to think about stain treatments wearing off
The room is a bedroom, playroom or family room rather than a stairway

blocks.title: Fiber is not the whole story:
blocks.text: Two nylon carpets can differ more from each other than nylon differs from polyester. Face weight, pile density and twist level decide how a carpet actually wears. When you compare samples, bend them back: if you see the backing easily through the pile, the carpet is thin regardless of fiber. We bring the density spec with every sample to a Sammamish carpet estimate.
Fiber mistakes we see in Sammamish homes

items.html: Soft polyester on the stairs. It feels wonderful in the showroom and mats on the top three treads within two years. Stairs need resilience first.
Wool in a house with a puppy. Urine changes the dye in wool and the mark is permanent. Wait until the dog is reliably trained, or choose a synthetic and save the wool for later.
Non-solution-dyed nylon in a south-facing bonus room. Big plateau windows fade carpet in stripes where the sun lands. Solution-dyed fiber, with color running through the strand, holds up far better.
Trusting the fiber name alone. Ask for face weight and density in writing. A common Reddit thread on carpet quality comes down to exactly this: two carpets, same fiber, very different construction.
Pairing a good fiber with a cheap pad. A quality nylon on a low-density pad wears like a cheap carpet. Match the pad to the fiber and the room.

faq.q: Which carpet fiber is the most durable?
faq.a: Nylon, followed closely by wool and triexta. Nylon fibers recover from foot traffic better than any other synthetic, which is why it dominates stairs and hallways. Wool matches it in resilience and outlasts it in years but needs more care. Polyester is the least durable in traffic even though it resists stains well.

It depends on the room. Triexta has permanent, built-in stain resistance and a softer feel, and its durability is close to nylon in normal family rooms and bedrooms. Nylon still has the edge on stairs and in long hallways where matting is the main risk. Many Sammamish homes we do use nylon on stairs and triexta everywhere else.

No, it is just misapplied often. Polyester resists stains, resists fading, feels soft and costs the least, which makes it a smart choice for bedrooms, guest rooms and offices. Its weakness is crushing in traffic lanes, so it disappoints on stairs and in busy halls. Buy it dense and put it in the right rooms.

faq.q: Is wool carpet worth the money?
faq.a: For a formal living room or a main bedroom in a home without young pets, often yes. Wool lasts two decades or more, hides soil, feels unlike any synthetic and is naturally flame resistant. It is not worth it in damp lower levels, in homes with untrained dogs, or in rooms where the budget is better spent on a dense nylon.

faq.q: What carpet fiber is best for pets?
faq.a: Triexta or solution-dyed nylon, paired with a moisture-barrier pad. Triexta's stain resistance is permanent and handles accidents well; solution-dyed nylon resists both fading and bleaching from enzyme cleaners. Avoid wool with pets that are not fully trained, and avoid loop styles that claws can snag.

faq.q: Does the fiber affect how much the carpet costs?
faq.a: It changes the material, not the labor. Polyester is generally the least expensive, nylon and triexta sit in the middle, and wool costs the most, often several times a basic polyester. Installation is $0.99 per sq ft stretched in and $30 per step whatever you choose, so we quote the carpet and pad separately at the free estimate.
